headline: AI-led liquidation hit every tracked name as the Friday session closed lower

entries.happened: AAPL closed at $342.56, -1.90% against the prior close, on 80,464,200 shares versus a trailing average of 47,701,275. Its range was $340.56 to $354.34. Research checked the company source list and Friday coverage; no new material company disclosure was verified for this session beyond the separately noted Nvidia SEC examination report. The measured bar does not establish a company-specific cause.
entries.why: The completed -1.90% return and volume comparison establish participation in Friday's broad risk-off session but not investor intent. The company-specific investment case still turns on revenue growth, margins, balance-sheet capacity and execution rather than one day of market action. A broad technology liquidation can move this stock at the same time as a dated disclosure without proving that the disclosure drove the bar. The next operating release and subsequent completed sessions are needed to distinguish valuation compression from a change in fundamentals.
entries.priced_in: At $342.56, the market has incorporated Friday's completed-session move, but the price does not reveal which future cash-flow or discount-rate assumption changed. The broad selloff is observable; a durable company-specific reset remains unproven.
entries.would_change: A dated filing, guidance update, customer or utilization metric, or subsequent trading pattern that changes expected revenue, margins, funding or cash flow would change this reading.

readthrough.heading: Cross-company interpretation
readthrough.title: Separate the measured liquidation from company evidence
readthrough.body: The twelve validated bars were all negative, with especially large declines in Nvidia, Nebius and Marvell. Friday's broad technology selloff and the reported SEC accounting examination involving Nvidia are dated context, but a price bar alone cannot prove causation for the other eleven names. The next company guidance, filings, utilization data and Monday breadth should test whether this was a one-session de-risking event or a durable reset in expected cash flows.
